native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies strongly and non-randomly among the ten habitat types of the Barcelona province, and the direction depends on the denominator, so both layers are required. Among the 191 of 632 plots that actually hold non-native plants (conditional layer; region-wide 169/481 records = 35.1%), the gardening share is highest in Wetlands (55.8%, 29/52, Wilson 95% CI 42.3-68.4) and Coastal (53.5%, 23/43, 38.9-67.5), intermediate in Riparian (36.5%), Meadows (30.8%) and Urban (29.8%, 45/151, 23.1-37.5), and lowest in Croplands (18.5%, 20/108, 12.3-26.9); habitat is associated with the gardening share (binomial GLM, LR chi2 = 50.6 on 9 df, asymptotic p = 8.2e-8, permutation p = 0.0002 from 5000 habitat-label shuffles). After Holm correction over the 15 contrasts meeting the >=10-records rule: Wetlands vs Croplands (OR 5.55, p_holm < 0.0001), Coastal vs Croplands (OR 5.06, p_holm = 0.0006), Wetlands vs Urban (OR 2.97, p_holm = 0.018); Riparian vs Croplands is suggestive only (OR 2.52, p_holm = 0.054). With all 632 plots as denominator (share of plots holding at least one gardening species) the ranking shifts because encounter rate differs tenfold: Urban 47.7% (36.0-59.6), Wetlands 50.0% (34.8-65.2), Coastal 44.8% (28.4-62.5), Riparian 36.1% (25.2-48.6), Croplands 20.7% (13.6-30.0), then Meadows 7.7%, Coniferous forests 6.5%, Broad-leaved forests 4.4%, Scrublands 1.9%, Rock outcrops 0% (0/57, 0-6.3); this association is stronger (LR chi2 = 146.9, 9 df, permutation p = 0.0002; 24 of 45 pairs Holm-significant). For Broad-leaved forests (4/4), Coniferous forests (7/8), Scrublands (2/5) and Rock outcrops (0/1) habitat-level record totals are 1-8, so their apparent 100%/87.5%/40%/0% is descriptive only and its direction is not interpreted - 0% in Rock outcrops means one non-native record in 57 plots, not absence of gardening introductions. Interpretation (labelled as interpretation): the pattern is consistent with gardening-derived species dominating the non-native pool where the overall non-native load is small but ornamental propagule pressure is near (waterways, wetlands, coasts), whereas the cropland pool is dominated by the unintentional seed-contaminant pathway (76.9% of its records); jointly the two layers imply gardening species are most likely to be encountered at all in urban and wetland habitats, while cropland records are the least gardening-derived. This is a post-hoc description, not a confirmatory test, and no causal verb is intended: there is no survey-effort variable and habitat is nearly collinear with the urbanisation gradient (mean urban cover, 1000 m buffer: Urban 0.50 vs Meadows 0.03), so habitat is not separable from that gradient in these data.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inventory (work/01_inspect.py, work/02_diag.py): discovered the two .csv files are TAB-separated; verified 632 plots (unique lon/lat), 10 habitat labels, zero NA, n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo == n.total in 632/632 rows, 441/632 plots with n.total=0, and absence of any species x habitat matrix (so the species table is context only, and the Newick tree is unused because the unit of analysis is the plot). 2) Two-layer descriptives with Wilson CIs (outputs/table1_descriptive_by_habitat.csv) and pathway composition per habitat (table6). 3) Main inference: binomial-logit GLM cbind(n.gard, n.other) ~ C(habitat) on the 191 plots with n.total>0, 10 levels, reference Urban, separated levels flagged (table2); omnibus LRT chi2=50.6 (9 df) plus 5000-permutation omnibus using a closed-form one-way binomial LR statistic verified to equal the GLM deviance difference (p=0.0002). 4) Post-hoc Fisher contrasts with Holm restricted to habitats with sum(n.total)>=10 (table3), and the same for the unconditional layer across all 10 habitats (table7). 5) Sensitivity/robustness (table4): presence-response on all 632 plots, quasi-binomial dispersion (scale 0.541, deviance/df 1.204, no overdispersion), collapsed semi-natural 5-level run, and covariate-adjusted runs with elevation + log(distance.road) + urban.2009.1000m / urban.2009.50m / cropland.2009.1000m. 6) Dominant-species check (top-3 gardening species = 28.8% of gardening records) and drop-one-plot jackknife of key contrasts (table8). 7) ASCII forest plot with Wilson CIs (figure1), headline stats (summary.json), manifest (README.md), hypothesis (hypothesis.md).

sub_hypo.text: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants introduced through gardening in the Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats; no direction of difference is specified.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.

sub_hypo.text: Among plots containing non-native plants, the proportion of non-native records attributable to gardening differs non-randomly among habitats, with the highest interpretable shares in Wetlands and Coastal habitats and the lowest in Croplands.
sub_hypo.context: Post-hoc, plot-level analysis of the 191 of 632 Barcelona province plots with n.total > 0, across ten habitat types; the regional conditional gardening share is 169/481 records (35.1%).
sub_hypo.relations: Conditional gardening share is sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) within habitat: Wetlands 55.8% (29/52; Wilson 95% CI 42.3–68.4), Coastal 53.5% (23/43; 38.9–67.5), Riparian 36.5%, Meadows 30.8%, Urban 29.8% (45/151; 23.1–37.5), and Croplands 18.5% (20/108; 12.3–26.9). Binomial-logit GLM association: LR chi-square 50.6, 9 df, asymptotic p = 8.2e-8; 5000 habitat-label permutations give p = 0.0002.

sub_hypo.text: Conditional gardening shares are significantly higher in Wetlands and Coastal habitats than in Croplands, and in Wetlands than in Urban habitats; the Riparian–Croplands difference is only suggestive.
sub_hypo.context: Post-hoc Fisher contrasts among Barcelona province habitats with at least ten non-native records per habitat, using the conditional layer and Holm correction across 15 contrasts.
sub_hypo.relations: Wetlands versus Croplands: OR 5.55, Holm p < 0.0001; Coastal versus Croplands: OR 5.06, Holm p = 0.0006; Wetlands versus Urban: OR 2.97, Holm p = 0.018. Riparian versus Croplands: OR 2.52, Holm p = 0.054, not Holm-significant.

sub_hypo.text: Across all plots, the probability of encountering at least one gardening-derived species differs strongly among habitats, with the highest occurrence in Wetlands and Urban habitats.
sub_hypo.context: Unconditional layer covering all 632 Barcelona province plots across ten habitats, including the 441 plots without non-native plants; post-hoc rather than confirmatory analysis.
sub_hypo.relations: The proportion of plots with n.gard > 0 is Wetlands 50.0% (Wilson 95% CI 34.8–65.2), Urban 47.7% (36.0–59.6), Coastal 44.8% (28.4–62.5), Riparian 36.1% (25.2–48.6), Croplands 20.7% (13.6–30.0), Meadows 7.7%, Coniferous forests 6.5%, Broad-leaved forests 4.4%, Scrublands 1.9%, and Rock outcrops 0% (0/57; 0–6.3). Habitat association is stronger than in the conditional layer: LR chi-square 146.9, 9 df, permutation p = 0.0002; 24 of 45 pairwise contrasts are Holm-significant.

sub_hypo.text: Habitat comparisons depend on whether gardening prevalence is measured among non-native records or among all plots, so both denominators are required.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison of conditional record composition in 191 occupied plots with unconditional gardening occurrence across all 632 Barcelona province plots.
sub_hypo.relations: Habitat rankings shift between sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) and the fraction of all plots with n.gard > 0 because encounter rates differ tenfold. Urban habitats have an intermediate conditional share (29.8%) but high unconditional occurrence (47.7%); jointly, the layers indicate gardening species are most likely encountered in Urban and Wetland habitats, while Cropland records are least gardening-derived.

sub_hypo.text: Conditional gardening shares in four sparsely represented habitats are descriptive only and do not support directional interpretation.
sub_hypo.context: Broad-leaved forests, Coniferous forests, Scrublands, and Rock outcrops in Barcelona province, each with only 1–8 non-native records.
sub_hypo.relations: Conditional shares are Broad-leaved forests 100% (4/4), Coniferous forests 87.5% (7/8), Scrublands 40% (2/5), and Rock outcrops 0% (0/1). Sparse denominators preclude interpreting their direction. Rock outcrops contain only one non-native record across 57 plots; the observed zero gardening share does not establish absence of gardening introductions.

sub_hypo.text: The observed pattern is consistent with gardening-derived species dominating small non-native pools near ornamental propagule sources, whereas Cropland records are dominated by unintentional introductions.
sub_hypo.context: Explicitly interpretive, non-causal, post-hoc description of Barcelona province habitats, particularly waterways, wetlands, coasts, and croplands.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening dominance where overall non-native load is small and ornamental propagule pressure is nearby is an interpretation, not a measured causal relationship. Unintentional introductions account for 76.9% of Cropland records, consistent with the stated seed-contaminant interpretation.

sub_hypo.text: The habitat association cannot be separated from the urbanisation gradient in these data and should not be interpreted causally.
sub_hypo.context: Post-hoc analysis of Barcelona province plots; no survey-effort variable is available. Sensitivity analyses included elevation, log distance to road, and alternative urban or cropland cover covariates.
sub_hypo.relations: Habitat is nearly collinear with urbanisation: mean urban cover within a 1000 m buffer is 0.50 in Urban habitats versus 0.03 in Meadows. Consequently, habitat and urbanisation effects are not separable here; no directional effects or successful removal of confounding are stated for the adjustment covariates.
